topic: From three spreadsheets to one system — what the first month of transition looked like
format: Open with a specific measurable result — a number, a time saved, a cost eliminated — then explain exactly what created it
post:
Week one: the payroll file crashed mid-run. Week four: WPS submitted in 11 minutes flat.

That gap — four weeks — is what moving from three spreadsheets to one system actually looked like for an operations team in Muscat.

Here's how it happened.

Month one was not smooth. Data was scattered across an HR sheet, a payroll file, and a WhatsApp group no one fully trusted. End-of-service gratuity calculations were done manually — one employee at a time. Ministry of Labour filings sat on a to-do list that rolled over weekly.

The first two weeks were migration. Painful, necessary.

By week three, WPS payroll Oman submissions were running through the platform with direct bank integration. SPF contributions auto-calculated. MOL filings queued and tracked — not chased.

Week four: the HR manager ran payroll for the full team, flagged two compliance gaps, and closed a work permit renewal — before lunch.

No extra vendor. No second system. No WhatsApp thread asking "did this go through?"

One platform. One source of truth.

If you're still deciding whether the switch is worth the disruption — the disruption is the point. The spreadsheet won't catch what it can't see.
